note: Anthropic gives the Claude 5 releases names rather than numbering them by size, so the name is most of what a reader has to go on. Below is what Anthropic says each name is for, quoted, and what ModelTree reads into it. The order is by first release, not by standing.

sources.title: Models overview
sources.quote: For complex agentic coding and enterprise work

editorial.summary: Anthropic scopes Opus by the kind of work — complex agentic coding, and enterprise deployment — rather than by a capability level. Whether that scope matches a particular workload is a question the wording leaves open.

sources.title: Models overview
sources.quote: The best combination of speed and intelligence

editorial.summary: Anthropic's wording for Sonnet is about a balance between how quickly it answers and how much reasoning it brings, stated across its own Claude 5 lineup and no wider. ModelTree reports the claim rather than testing it.

Anthropic frames Fable around agent runs that continue over a long horizon rather than around a single exchange. That describes the shape of the work, and says nothing about where Fable falls against the other Claude 5 names.

note: Claude 4.5 is recorded here with a single variant, so its naming settles what Haiku is for in this generation and nothing about how the same name reads in another one.

sources.title: Models overview
sources.quote: The fastest model with near-frontier intelligence

editorial.summary: Anthropic's description of Haiku pairs a latency claim with a hedge on reasoning — near the frontier rather than at it. ModelTree keeps the hedge, because it is the part a quick reading of the name tends to drop.

note: Google's wording for these two names is explicitly scoped to the 2.5 family, and ModelTree keeps that scope: the readings below apply to the releases in this family and are not carried forward to a later generation.

sources.title: Gemini API models
sources.quote: Our most advanced model for complex tasks, featuring deep reasoning and coding capabilities in the 2.5 family.

editorial.summary: Google qualifies the claim with the words "in the 2.5 family", and that qualifier is the useful part of it: the wording places Pro among the 2.5 releases and reaches no further than them.

sources.title: Gemini API models
sources.quote: Our best price-performance model for low-latency, high-volume tasks that require reasoning.

editorial.summary: Google's Flash wording covers two things at once: how quickly a response comes back, and what it takes to run a great many of them. ModelTree reads the latency and volume half; the commercial half is a separate fact, recorded elsewhere with its own sources and dates.

note: Gemini 3 carries three variant names across several releases, and a name here covers every release in this family that uses it. Google states the positioning for the series; ModelTree does not extend it to any other Gemini generation.

sources.title: Gemini 3 developer guide
sources.quote: best for complex tasks that require broad world knowledge and advanced reasoning across modalities

editorial.summary: Google describes Pro here in terms of breadth — world knowledge, and reasoning that spans modalities. This is the Gemini 3 wording; Google words Gemini 2.5 Pro differently, which is why the two generations are recorded apart.

sources.title: Gemini 3 developer guide
sources.quote: Gemini 3 Flash is our latest 3-series model, with Pro-level intelligence at the speed and pricing of Flash.

editorial.summary: Google defines Flash by reference to Pro inside the same series — a comparison drawn within one family rather than a rung on a ladder. ModelTree carries the wording as stated and adds no ordering of its own.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
sources.quote: a low-latency, cost-effective multimodal model optimized for high-frequency, lightweight tasks

editorial.summary: Google's Flash-Lite wording is about running a great deal of work rather than about how hard any single piece of it is. ModelTree reads that as a claim about throughput, not as a statement that Flash-Lite reasons less well than its siblings.
